exposure: mode of birth (vaginal vs. cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study included 100 women who underwent childbirth (50 vaginal and 50 cesarean deliveries) at a multispecialty hospital and were administered carbetocin immediately postpartum.
finding: Carbetocin was highly effective in preventing postpartum hemorrhage, with high success rates and a favorable safety profile in both vaginal and cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: While effective in both, carbetocin showed a slightly higher PPH prevention success rate in cesarean deliveries (96%) compared to vaginal deliveries (90%), and the need for additional uterotonics was significantly lower in the cesarean group.
